criterion: The introduction sentence on the dive stays legible as the water brightens behind the sentence.
evaluation_rule: The introduction sentence is the one line of prose centred over open water in the second scene. Watch the sentence for several seconds as brighter bands of light pass behind the sentence. Yes if the sentence remains readable at every moment, turning dark where the water turns bright, with nothing drawn behind the sentence. No if the sentence becomes hard to read at any moment, or if a dark box or scrim sits behind the sentence.

criterion: A single element across every surface of the product wears the mid, vivid orange signal colour.
evaluation_rule: The signal colour is the one warm amber orange in an otherwise blue-green and white interface. Walk the dive, the logbook, the dock and a refusal surface looking for that orange. Yes if one element in the whole product wears the orange, with every other emphasis made from how solid the white ink is. No if two or more elements wear the orange, or if the orange appears nowhere.

criterion: The pointer the dive draws for itself changes appearance when the pointer passes over something that can be activated.
evaluation_rule: Inside the dive the system pointer is hidden and the site draws its own pointer. Move that pointer across open water, then over one of the three header words. Yes if the drawn pointer looks one way over water and visibly different over the header word. No if the drawn pointer looks identical in both places, or if the system pointer is showing instead.

criterion: A machine lacking graphics hardware shows the dive as a still frame of water beneath the full text of the site.
evaluation_rule: Open the dive with hardware acceleration switched off. Yes if the water renders as one motionless dark blue-green field, every scene's words still appear as the visitor descends, and the visitor is told nothing about the downgrade. No if an error surface appears instead, or if the water layer vanishes and leaves the words on bare ground.

criterion: The water behind every scene of the dive drifts on the water's own clock, bending further under a fast sweep of the pointer.
evaluation_rule: The water is the moving underwater field behind every scene of the dive. Keep the pointer still for ten seconds, then sweep the pointer quickly across the water. Yes if the water keeps moving while the pointer is still, then distorts locally under the fast sweep. No if the water is frozen while the pointer is still, or if a fast sweep leaves the water unchanged.

criterion: On the dive, the three bars inside the audio control rise with the sound the site is playing.
evaluation_rule: The audio control is the small circle at the bottom right of the dive holding three vertical bars. Enter with audio, watch the bars, then switch the audio off with the same control. Yes if the bars move in time with the sound while the sound plays, then hold still once the sound stops. No if the bars animate on a fixed loop whatever the sound does, or if the bars never move.

criterion: The corner controls of the dive arrive on screen once the introduction has completed.
evaluation_rule: The corner controls are the monogram at the top left, the three words at the top right, the audio circle at the bottom right and the save control at the bottom left. Enter the dive and watch the four corners from the first frame. Yes if the corners are empty while the introduction plays, then the corner controls fade up once the introduction ends. No if the corner controls are present from the first frame, or if the corner controls never appear.

criterion: The entry gate of the dive presents entering with sound, entering in silence, as two equal choices.
evaluation_rule: The entry gate is the screen that replaces the loading meter before the dive begins, offering Dive into the experience and Enter without audio. Look at how the two controls sit on the screen. Yes if the two read as two genuine ways in, placed well apart, each one plainly a way to enter. No if the second reads as a small disclaimer tucked under the first, or if only one way in is offered.

criterion: The water in every scene of the dive reads as a deep, soft teal that fades toward near-black with distance.
evaluation_rule: The water is the moving underwater field behind every scene of the dive. Look at the near water and at the far distance in three different scenes. Yes if the near water is a deep, soft teal and distant shapes dissolve into a near-black blue-green rather than simply shrinking. No if the water reads as another hue such as bright blue or grey, or if distant shapes stay as crisp as near ones.

criterion: The loading surface of the dive dissolves into the first scene over one unchanging ground colour.
evaluation_rule: The loading surface is the dark screen with the bracketed waiting label and the row of slash characters that shows before the dive. Reload the dive and watch the moment the loading surface gives way. Yes if the loading surface fades over a ground that keeps the same dark colour, so only the water's shapes appear. No if the screen flashes a different colour at the handover, or if the loading surface vanishes in a single frame.

criterion: The water surges hardest at the midpoint of a change from one scene of the dive to the next.
evaluation_rule: A scene change is the moment the dive passes from one scene's words to the next scene's words. Gesture once and watch the water rather than the words. Yes if the distortion builds to a peak while neither scene's words are readable, then settles once the new scene is legible. No if the water keeps one constant amount of distortion through the change, or if the peak lands at the start or the end.

criterion: A form control on the sign-in surface stays readable during the moment the control waits on a request.
evaluation_rule: The sign-in surface is the dark form reached from the save control, with the bracketed surface log label above its fields. Submit the form and look at the controls during the moment the request is in flight. Yes if every label stays readable against the dark ground, with a spinner showing that the control is busy. No if a label fades until the label is hard to read, or if the only sign of the busy state is that faintness.

criterion: The two-line rights block at the foot of the dive's contact deck reads at arm's length at a phone width.
evaluation_rule: The rights block is the two lines of small print at the very foot of the last scene of the dive. Open the dive at a phone width and descend to the last scene. Yes if both lines can be read at arm's length without zooming, with neither line running off the screen. No if the print is too small to read without zooming, or if either line overflows the screen.
